purpose: Classify RedCap's current asset classes before any LLM-wiki-lite implementation, so semantic memory helps AI and humans without replacing control truth, leaking private evidence, or bypassing RedCap Forge.

asset_layers.reason: Live task scope, promises, drift sentinels, and completion truth must remain machine-checkable and cannot become synthesized memory.
Entry files and host contracts may be explained by wiki pages, but the executable/importable surfaces remain authoritative.
Policies are control truth. A wiki page may explain a policy family with source anchors, but cannot override policy JSON or markdown.
Executable scripts and dispatchers are code. Wiki can document behavior but cannot store or replace runnable logic.
Current reports are private evidence. Stable lessons may be distilled from them, but raw reports are not wiki content.

file_level_rules.reason: Stable design philosophy is a strong semantic-memory candidate.
Repeated failure patterns and reusable fixes are strong semantic-memory candidates after dedupe and source anchoring.
Append-only chronology is source evidence for memory updates, not a wiki page itself.
Host behavior changes over time; wiki entries derived from it must expire quickly.
Useful as conceptual synthesis, but must stay anchored because control mechanisms evolve.

asset_layers.reason: Cold archaeology remains private evidence. Wiki synthesis may cite it only through anchors after privacy and dedupe review.
Formal Prism reports are evidence and verdict records. Wiki may summarize stable conclusions but not replace the report.
Raw Prism outputs are local evidence with high privacy and token risk; only distilled conclusions may become candidates.
Evolution candidates and identity proposals are pipeline state. Wiki can use promoted candidate conclusions, not raw candidate queues.
This is the template for public redcap-arsenal entries, not the private LLM-wiki store.
Public entries are produced by RedCap Forge. They may later feed wiki summaries, but private wiki must not write directly to this layer.
Indexes route reads and prevent token blowups. Wiki must be indexed by them, not replace them.
Package identity and legal surfaces are release contracts; wiki can explain them but not serve as authority.

llm_wiki_candidate_types.rule: Wiki may cache derived preference summaries, but identity.md remains the source of truth and identity changes must expire derived wiki entries.
Must include problem source, solution, final effect, and source anchors.
Must cite original policy/report anchors and mark whether it is advisory or mandatory.

llm_wiki_candidate_types.reason: Current task state belongs to .dev-task.md and closeout runtime.
Raw private evidence must not be copied into wiki.
Code belongs to runtime files; wiki may explain behavior only.

source_anchor_contract.raw_excerpt_rule: Do not inline raw private passages into wiki entries; cite source anchors and paraphrase safely.
source_anchor_contract.staleness_rule: A wiki entry is stale when any required source anchor no longer resolves, its commit/digest no longer matches, or its source policy has changed since last_reviewed_at.

forge_required_for: skill candidates derived from private reports

retrieval_boundary.must_not_claim: LLM-wiki is not a replacement for source-path-preserving retrieval.

registered_followup_requirement.title: LLM-wiki-lite semantic memory lifecycle implementation
registered_followup_requirement.reason: After asset stratification, RedCap can implement a private, source-anchored, non-authoritative semantic memory layer without enabling public writeback, RAG, GraphRAG, or raw private export.
out_of_scope: rewriting existing control policies as wiki pages

must_not_claim: Do not claim P4-2h-2 implements a complete LLM-wiki system.
Do not claim LLM-wiki is a source of truth.
Do not claim raw private reports, Prism runs, identity, or runtime evidence are safe wiki content.
Do not claim LLM-wiki replaces catalog + rg + metadata retrieval.
Do not claim public redcap-arsenal entries can be written without RedCap Forge.
Do not claim RAG or GraphRAG is enabled by this policy.
